headline: A Los Angeles radio station's AI co-host, Coyotec, now shares a weekday show with a human DJ, while the actors' union SAG-AFTRA and other critics warn that AI hosts threaten jobs and listener trust.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a concrete case of AI in broadcasting with a mixed picture, but one station and its own audience claims.
importance_line: Radio hosts and other broadcast workers are affected first (U.S. radio jobs fell about 22% between 2019 and 2025, per the article), then listeners who may trust an AI voice, then station owners; the audience gains are the station’s own claim and the cause is unclear.
summary: The Los Angeles Times reports that José FM, a Spanish-language station owned by Entravision, pairs a human DJ, Geraldine Guzman, with Coyotec, an AI character whose voice was built with ElevenLabs technology, and that the show has moved to weekday commuting hours and spread to other cities. The station says its audience grew, but it is unclear whether that is because of the DJ, the AI or both, and the actors’ union SAG-AFTRA and other critics warn that AI hosts erode trust and jobs.
notes: Single-outlet feature; the audience gains are the station's own claim, and the article says the cause is unclear. Feature about an ongoing trend, so marked NEW as a report, not a follow-up.
